name: Rendering Pipelines and Passes
text:
# Rendering Pipelines and Passes

Also called: Render Forward Pass

## Overview
Rendering Pipelines and Passes refers to the architectural organization of volume rendering into discrete, sequential stages or passes, typically leveraging hardware-accelerated rasterization to transform volumetric primitives into a 2D image [S1, S3, S4, unofficial]. It solves the performance bottleneck of [direct volume rendering](#1184-direct-volume-rendering.md) by decomposing the complex task of visibility determination, shading, and [compositing](#2436-compositing.md) into manageable, reusable components [S1, S2, S3, unofficial]. Unlike monolithic ray-marching shaders or single-pass [splatting](#23-splatting.md) implementations, this family explicitly separates geometry traversal, attribute computation, and final screen presentation, enabling complex effects like deferred shading, differentiable optimization, and efficient memory management [S1, S2, unofficial][S10, abstract only, unofficial].

## Shared principles
The rendering pipeline family shares the fundamental mechanism of treating volumetric data as a set of geometric or parametric primitives that are transformed and rasterized [S1, S3, S4, unofficial].

1.  **Primitive Representation:** The volume is decomposed into primitives. These may be explicit geometric shapes (cubes, cells, splats) or implicit functions sampled via texture hardware [S1, S3, S4, unofficial]. Each primitive $k$ is defined by its position $\mathbf{p}_k$, density/extinction coefficient $g_k$ or $\rho_k$, and a reconstruction kernel $h$ (typically a Gaussian) [S1, unofficial][S6, unofficial][S10, abstract only, unofficial].
2.  **Transformation:** Primitives are transformed from volume space to screen space using the Model-View-Projection (MVP) matrix or specific factorizations (e.g., [shear-warp](#24-shear-warp.md)) [S2, S3, S4, unofficial]. For perspective projections, the kernel shape may be distorted (e.g., [EWA splatting](#1069-ewa-splatting.md)) to account for foreshortening [S6, unofficial][S10, abstract only, unofficial].
3.  **Rasterization:** The transformed primitives are projected onto the 2D image plane. This step leverages hardware-accelerated scan-conversion, depth testing, and blending [S1, S2, S3, S4, unofficial]. The contribution of a voxel $D$ to a screen point $(x,y)$ is determined by the [footprint function](#4731-footprint-function-mechanism.md) $F(x,y)$, which is the integral of the 3D kernel along the view direction [S2, unofficial][S6, unofficial][S10, abstract only, unofficial]:
    $$ F(x,y) = \int h(x-x_D, y-y_D, z) \, dz $$
    The intensity written to the pixel is modulated by the voxel density:
    $$ P(x,y) = \text{weight}(x,y) \cdot \rho(D) $$
    where $\text{weight}(x,y) = F(x-x_D, y-y_D)$ [S10, abstract only, unofficial].
4.  **Compositing:** Contributions are accumulated to form the final image. This is typically done using [alpha blending](#5750-alpha-blending.md) in back-to-front or front-to-back order to handle transparency correctly [S1, S2, S3, unofficial][S7]. Splatting compositing is performed along sheets (all pixels at once for a set of voxels), whereas ray-casting composites along rays (one sample at a time) [S10, abstract only, unofficial].
5.  **Hardware [Acceleration](#18-acceleration.md):** Most methods in this family rely on GPU rasterization pipelines for performance, enabling real-time interactivity [S1, S2, S3, unofficial].

## Subtopics

### [Plug-and-Play Ray Marching and Rendering](981-plug-and-play-ray-marching-and-rendering.md)
A modular interface that decouples [ray marching](#6739-ray-marching.md) and differentiable rendering logic from the radiance field representation, allowing any user-defined field (e.g., MLPs) to be plugged into a standardized acceleration engine via two query functions. It differs from monolithic implementations like [Instant-NGP](#6604-instant-ngp.md) by providing a Python API built on PyTorch for easier extension to dynamic scenes and custom architectures.

### [Time-Sliced Pipelined Architecture](1435-time-sliced-pipelined-architecture.md)
A hardware design methodology that achieves real-time performance by time-slicing functional blocks (sub-cores) to allow simultaneous processing of multiple tasks, solving the bottleneck of sequential execution. It integrates reusable sub-cores into a multi-core structure (often in ASIC/FPGA) to handle shear-warp factorization efficiently, unlike general-purpose DSP solutions.

### [Slice-by-Slice (Sheet Buffer) Splatting](2110-slice-by-slice-sheet-buffer-splatting.md)
An optimization that organizes splats into cache-sheets aligned parallel to the volume face most parallel to the image plane, compositing these sheets slice-by-slice. It leverages hardware-accelerated rasterization for bulk accumulation within 2D planes, avoiding the "sparkling" artifacts of multi-view splatting at the cost of potential "popping" artifacts when view angles change.

### [Screen Quad Rendering](2435-screen-quad-rendering.md)
The final compositing stage in a multi-pass pipeline, responsible for displaying accumulated volume data from intermediate framebuffers onto the screen. It explicitly separates volume traversal/compositing logic from final screen presentation, relying on hardware-accelerated rasterization of a fullscreen primitive rather than software-based ray traversal.

### [Rendering Pipeline Architecture](3059-rendering-pipeline-architecture.md)
A family of object-order methods that decompose volumetric data into primitives (splats) which are transformed, rasterized, and composited. It solves the performance bottleneck of volume rendering by leveraging hardware-accelerated rasterization and blending, enabling real-time interactivity for dense point sets or voxel data.

### [Custom Pass Rendering](3629-custom-pass-rendering.md)
A multi-pass, object-order pipeline designed for high-performance visualization of large-scale volumetric data (NanoVDB) and octree-based geometry. It decouples geometric traversal from shading by using a sequence of specialized FullScreenPass stages to build intermediate G-buffers (hit position, filtered normals, ambient occlusion) before a final shading pass.

### [Multi-View Splatting Pipeline with Fill-Rate Filtering](4689-multi-view-splatting-pipeline-with-fill-rate-filtering.md)
A method that generates multi-view 2D images from a 3D point cloud by splatting points onto image planes and filtering out sparse views based on fill rate. It integrates a post-rendering quality control step that discards views with insufficient pixel coverage, ensuring structured, high-quality outputs for dataset generation.

### [DirectXSplat Renderer API](8504-directxsplat-renderer-api.md)
A C++/Direct3D 12 library for rendering 3D Gaussian Splats, providing a rasterization pipeline with explicit resource management. It exposes a host-owned device, queue, command list, and fence architecture, giving the application full control over the D3D12 submission loop while managing [Gaussian splat rasterization](#3253-gaussian-splat-rasterization-vertex-shader.md) internally, achieving up to 2.4x higher frame rates than some alternatives.

### [Ray-Centric and Hardware-Accelerated Rendering](8936-ray-centric-and-hardware-accelerated-rendering.md)
A ray-order method that computes pixel color by tracing rays through the volume, sampling density, and compositing along the ray path. It avoids the sorting and blending artifacts inherent in splatting methods while leveraging GPU hardware acceleration for real-time performance.

### [Multi-Pass and Sequential Stage Architectures](10539-multi-pass-and-sequential-stage-architectures.md)
An approach that decomposes volume rendering into discrete, ordered processing steps executed across multiple rendering passes. It solves the complexity of integrating diverse operations by decoupling them into specialized stages, allowing intermediate data (e.g., fragment lists, G-buffers) to be stored and processed between stages for complex effects like deferred shading.

### Image-order Splatting
An image-order approach that improves accuracy when using a perspective projection by processing pixels rather than primitives [S2, unofficial].

## Background
The concept of rendering pipelines in volume visualization has evolved from early software-based [ray casting](#6080-ray-casting.md) to hardware-accelerated splatting and modern multi-pass deferred shading techniques. The foundational work on splatting, such as Westover's volume splatting, introduced the idea of mapping view-dependent footprints to generic tables to improve speed [S2, unofficial]. Later developments, such as the shear-warp factorization, enabled efficient hardware implementation of volume rendering pipelines [S1, unofficial]. The rise of [neural radiance fields](#4972-neural-radiance-fields.md) (NeRFs) and 3D [Gaussian Splatting](#946-gaussian-splatting.md) has further driven the development of modular, differentiable, and highly optimized rendering pipelines that separate scene representation from rendering logic [S1, unofficial]. These methods are widely used in real-time visualization, scientific imaging, and computer graphics training pipelines.
